describe: the shoulder beside an intercity road's carriageway, where a city street would have its pavement: packed gravel and compacted dirt seen straight down, with no lines, ruts or direction of any kind

looks.describe: a gravel road shoulder: compacted grey-beige crushed stone fines packed hard and flat, densely scattered small grey and buff stones one to three centimetres across, soft broad patches of slightly darker packed earth
the same gravel shoulder a little more used: drier and dustier, a shade browner, more packed earth showing between the stones, still flat, no plants
